strengths: Top DEGs include MAFA, a canonical mature beta-cell/islet endocrine transcription factor, plus G6PC3 and HDC, supporting an endocrine rather than exocrine identity.
Pancreas tissue context and absence of canonical acinar digestive enzymes (PRSS1, CPA1, CELA3A, AMY2A) favor islet endocrine lineage.
weaknesses: Top-level label is broad and no definitive islet hormone genes (INS, GCG) are in the marker list.
CASSIA mapping was ambiguous/unmapped in the frozen registry, although a proposed CL:0008024 was available.

strengths: Some observed DEGs (KCNK2, SCN3B, ROBO1, NAV3, FGF14) have neural/neuroendocrine associations.
weaknesses: No glial-specific markers (SOX10, PLP1, MBP, S100B) are present.
MAFA, G6PC3, HDC and the pancreas tissue context strongly favor endocrine over neural/glial identity; neural-like genes are shared/ambiguous and do not distinguish a glial branch.

strengths: Provides a deterministic ontology mapping to CL:0002064.
SERPINH1 and CRISPLD2 were noted as possible acinar-associated genes, though neither is a canonical acinar marker.
weaknesses: Canonical acinar markers (PRSS1, CPA1, CELA3A, AMY2A) are absent from the DEG list.
Enrichment terms are mostly generic transport/metabolic pathways and do not specifically support acinar identity.
MAFA, G6PC3 and HDC favor pancreatic endocrine rather than exocrine identity.

supporting: Top DEGs MAFA, G6PC3 and HDC support pancreatic islet/endocrine identity.
Absence of canonical exocrine digestive enzymes (PRSS1, CPA1, CELA3A, AMY2A) argues against acinar identity.
Pancreas tissue context supports islet endocrine lineage over neural/glial identity.
conflicting: Neural/glial label is not supported by glial-specific markers and conflicts with MAFA/G6PC3/HDC endocrine signals.
Acinar label is not supported by canonical acinar digestive enzyme markers.
Enrichment terms are generic transport/metabolic pathways (ABC transporters, small molecule transport) and do not resolve endocrine vs exocrine identity.
